name: full
description: The rich profile plus every WinUI3 type that the WinUI 3 Gallery port (samples/Gallery) builds its pages from and the smaller profiles leave out. The port is meant to show that the whole Gallery can be written without XAML, with the same types, so this file grows by one group per stage of the porting plan, never by a type nobody asked for.

packages.comment: WrapPanel and LayoutPanel: the stable WinUI package keeps them out of Microsoft.UI.Xaml.winmd, this channel declares them. The whole WinUI metadata and style catalogue are read from it, the rest of the release is the stable one. tools/packages.json pins the same version for tools/restore-packages.ps1.
System and Shell pages: what the Windows App SDK adds outside the UI -- the badge of the taskbar button, the notifications, the storage pickers.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.UserControl.comment: The base of the Gallery's own controls (ControlExample, PageHeader) and of Page. Whole surface.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Page.comment: The page the Gallery's Frame shows. Never created by Frame.Navigate here -- that takes a TypeName of a XAML class -- but built directly and put into Frame.Content.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Frame.comment: The Gallery's rootFrame and the Frame of its sample pages.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.NavigationVie.comment: The "Controls" caption between the Gallery navigation view's groups.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.GridView.comment: The tile grid of the Gallery's Home, All controls and section pages. Everything a ListViewBase gives (selection mode, item click) comes from base.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.BitmapIcon.comment: The Gallery's navigation group icon when the catalogue names a .png.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ImageIcon.comment: An icon from an image source.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ImageIconSour.comment: The icon a TitleBar carries beside its title.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TitleBar.comment: IconSource on top of what extended asks for: the Gallery's window icon in its title bar. RecomputeDragRegions: the regions that drag and the regions that take clicks, worked out again after content is added to or removed from the title bar at run time; AutoRefreshDragRegions says whether that is done without being asked.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.NavigationVie.comment: What the Gallery's main window asks of its navigation view beyond base and extended: whether the pane is an overlay or expanded, and the toggle the title bar takes over.
The group rows: they expand and are not themselves a page.
Which item the selection landed on.
Which item was clicked, a group row included: SelectsOnInvoked false rows raise only this.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.AutoSuggestBo.comment: The search box in the Gallery's title bar: its query icon, and the text of the query it submits.
What was typed when the query was submitted.
Why the text changed: only a user's typing refreshes suggestions.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Primitives.Re.comment: Basic input: fires Click again and again while it is held.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ToggleSplitBu.comment: Basic input: a SplitButton whose main part toggles.
Carries nothing of its own; the new state is read from the button.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ColorPicker.comment: Basic input: the colour picker page turns each of its parts on and off and reads the colour back.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RatingControl.comment: Basic input: stars, with a caption, a placeholder value and clearing.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Slider.comment: Ticks and their snapping on top of what base asks for.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ComboBox.comment: The text of an editable box and the moment it is submitted.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ComboBoxTextS.comment: What was typed, and whether the handler took it over.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.VariableSized.comment: The swatch grid of the SplitButton text example, and the Layout group's own page: the size of a cell, and the spans an item takes.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.InfoBadge.comment: Status & info: the badge, whole -- its value, its icon, its dot.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.FontIconSourc.comment: Status & info: the icon an InfoBadge takes as a glyph of a font.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.InfoBar.comment: Status & info: the one button an InfoBar carries, and the content under its message (Windowing: the warning with formatted text).

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ToolTip.comment: Status & info: where a tip stands, and the rectangle it keeps clear.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.UIElement.comment: Status & info: a tip that is an element of its own (ToolTipService.ToolTip over an object), beside toolTip, which is the text. Layout: Measure and Arrange, which a custom layout calls on its children.

IsDragRegion.comment: Windowing: whether an element in a TitleBar drags the window (true), takes clicks (false) or leaves the choice to the TitleBar (empty) -- TitleBar.IsDragRegion, the attached property.

ToolTipElement.comment: The tip as a ToolTip element: content that is not text, a placement, an offset. The hover half of toolTip only -- an element has no words to give a screen reader.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Input.KeyboardAccelera.comment: Menus & toolbars: the key chord that invokes a command, written beside the command.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.PathIcon.comment: Menus & toolbars: an icon drawn from a path.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.CommandBar.comment: Menus & toolbars: a bar that stays open until told to close, and says when it opens and closes (the user does that too, with the ellipsis).

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ICommandBarEl.comment: Menus & toolbars: what a command bar holds -- AppBarButton, AppBarToggleButton, AppBarSeparator -- which has no class of its own, only this interface.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.RadialGradientBr.comment: Styles: what the base profile leaves out of the radial brush -- how the gradient continues past its last stop.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.AnimatedIcon.comment: Styles: an icon that plays an animation as its state changes -- the state is set by name, "PointerOver" and "Normal" by the control it sits in or by hand.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.IAnimatedVisu.comment: Styles: what an AnimatedIcon plays -- any of the animated visuals below.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.AnimatedVisua.comment: Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.
Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.
Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.
Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.
Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.
Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.
Styles: an animation of the set the Gallery plays in an AnimatedIcon.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.AcrylicBrush.comment: Styles: in-app acrylic -- frosted glass over what is behind it in the window, with a tint and a colour to fall back on where the effect is switched off.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.ResourceDictionary.comment: Resources: values looked up by key from the element down -- a dictionary merged from a file (Source, MergedDictionaries) and entries written in place (Entry). The framework's own density dictionary and the page's overrides of one key are how the Gallery's Compact Sizing page works.

Entry.comment: One key and its value. The same tag repeated adds one entry each.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.AppWindow.comment: Windowing: the size of the client area in physical pixels, independent of the frame around it; the icon of the taskbar and the icon of the title bar, each by itself.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.PersonPicture.comment: Windowing: the round avatar the title bar of the Gallery windows carries -- the initials of the person.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.AppWindowTitleBar.comment: Windowing: the colours of the caption itself, active and inactive; the colours of its buttons are already asked for by extended.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.OverlappedPresent.comment: Windowing: a presenter made for a dialog -- a window that is not a main one -- beside the ordinary one extended asks for.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.CompactOverlayPre.comment: Windowing: a small window that stays above all others (picture-in-picture), and how big it starts.

Microsoft.Windows.BadgeNotifications.Bad.comment: System: the badge on the application's taskbar button -- a count or a glyph, set and cleared. It needs a packaged application: an unpackaged one has no taskbar identity for the shell to put it on.

Microsoft.Windows.AppNotifications.AppNo.comment: System: the notifications of the application in the shell -- shown as toasts, kept in the notification centre. The application registers with the shell once, and may show after that.
System: one notification, built by the builder.

Microsoft.Windows.AppNotifications.Build.comment: System: the builder of a notification: texts, an image, a sound, a time, controls. Each call returns the builder, so a notification reads as one chain.
System: a button on a notification, with the arguments it hands back to the application.
System: a list on a notification.
System: a progress bar on a notification.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.Geometry.comment: Shapes: the abstract geometry. A string of the path language of XAML builds one, as `data = u"M 10,100 H 200"` does; the framework's own converter makes the object.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.LineGeometry.comment: Shapes: a segment between two points.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.EllipseGeometry.comment: Shapes: an ellipse by its centre and radii.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.RectangleGeometr.comment: Shapes: a rectangle by its Rect.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Shapes.Line.comment: Shapes: a straight line between two points.

Points.comment: The vertices as text, in the form of XAML: points = u"10,100 60,40 200,40". Points is a collection of Point that wxl has no class for; the framework's own converter reads the text.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Shapes.Polygon.comment: Shapes: connected straight lines that close.

Points.comment: The vertices as text, in the form of XAML: points = u"10,100 60,40 200,40". Points is a collection of Point that wxl has no class for; the framework's own converter reads the text.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Shapes.Path.comment: Shapes: a shape drawn from a geometry.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.WrapPanel.comment: Layout: items that flow and wrap.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.LayoutPanel.comment: Layout: a panel that places its children by a layout object.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.StackLayout.comment: Layout: the layout LayoutPanel gets beside a custom one.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollViewer.comment: Gallery: the chaining of a viewer that cannot scroll, and a code block in a horizontal ScrollViewer must not keep the wheel from the page around it.

WheelToParent.comment: A wheel turn this viewer cannot use (nothing to scroll up or down, no modifier key) goes on up to the panel that scrolls the page. The viewer takes the wheel and marks it handled even when it scrolls nothing, so without this a horizontal strip of code stops the page.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RadioMenuFlyo.comment: Menus & toolbars: a menu item that is one of a group, checked like a radio button.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SplitMenuFlyo.comment: Menus & toolbars: a menu item with a submenu beside its own action.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.CommandBarFly.comment: Menus & toolbars: a command bar in a flyout.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SwipeControl.comment: Menus & toolbars: items revealed or invoked by swiping. LeftItems and RightItems are the collections themselves (SwipeItems is a vector and wxl stands it for the collection), so the Mode the class carries has a property of its own here.

LeftItemsMode.comment: SwipeItems.Mode of the left items: Reveal shows the buttons, Execute runs the first on a full swipe.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SwipeItemInvo.comment: Menus & toolbars: which control the item was invoked on.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SwipeItems.comment: Menus & toolbars: a group of swipe actions and what invoking one does.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Input.XamlUICommand.comment: Menus & toolbars: a command shared by every control that shows it.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Input.StandardUIComman.comment: Menus & toolbars: a command the system names and gives a glyph and a key.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SymbolIconSou.comment: Menus & toolbars: the symbol of a command or swipe item.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.BitmapIconSou.comment: Menus & toolbars: the bitmap of a command or swipe item.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Primitives.Fl.comment: Menus & toolbars: how a flyout is shown -- where it stands and whether it takes the focus.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Input.ExecuteRequested.comment: Menus & toolbars: what a command was asked to run with.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Input.Pointer.comment: Menus & toolbars: a hover button shows for a mouse or a pen and not for a finger, which has no hover.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.DatePicker.comment: Date & time: the date and what of it is shown.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TimePicker.comment: Date & time: the clock and how finely minutes go.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.CalendarView.comment: Date & time: the month calendar the Gallery's CalendarView page shows.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.PagerControl.comment: Scrolling: a pager for a count of pages, bounded or not.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.PipsPager.comment: Scrolling: dots for the pages of a flip view or a list.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollView.comment: Scrolling: the ScrollViewer of the compositor, with programmatic scrolling. The scroll controllers of its presenter are properties of the view here, given an AnnotatedScrollBar.

VerticalScrollController.comment: The bar that drives the view up and down, and is told where it is.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.AnnotatedScro.comment: Scrolling: where the pointer is on the rail, and what to show there.
Scrolling: a scroll bar with labels along it.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SemanticZoom.comment: Scrolling: two views of one collection, close and far.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollingScro.comment: Scrolling: the animation a programmatic scroll is about to run, which the handler may replace.
Scrolling: how a programmatic scroll goes -- animated or at once, and whether it snaps.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ScrollingZoom.comment: Scrolling: the same for a programmatic zoom.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.NumberBoxValu.comment: Scrolling: the value before and after, which a velocity box turns round on.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.ThemeShadow.comment: Styles: the elements a theme shadow falls on.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SplitView.comment: Layout: the pane's own paint, which the page changes from a list.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Viewbox.comment: Layout: what the viewbox holds and how it stretches it.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RelativePanel.comment: Layout: the panel, and every attached property its children are placed by -- against a sibling or against the panel.

Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextDocument.comment: The selection: SplitButton and ToggleSplitButton pages format it.

Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.comment: Text and paragraph formatting of a range (and so of a selection).

Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextSelection.comment: What Document.Selection hands out: a range with a caret. Everything it does comes from ITextRange.

Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextParagraphFormat.comment: The marker of a list paragraph (bullets, Roman numerals).

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.FrameworkElement.comment: AllowFocusOnInteraction: a button that opens a flyout holding an input keeps focus when pressed. Parent: a handler reads its siblings from the panel it is in, so that no handler has to capture an element (a captured sibling that captures back is a cycle nothing breaks).

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Primitives.Fl.comment: Target: the element a flyout is attached to. A coroutine started when the flyout opens finds its owner there, so no handler has to capture the owner (which holds the flyout: a cycle).

Windows.ApplicationModel.DataTransfer.Cl.comment: The copy button under every example puts the code on the clipboard; the Clipboard page of the Gallery reads it back, clears it, asks whether its history and roaming are on, puts content with options, and hears it change.

Windows.ApplicationModel.DataTransfer.Da.comment: What goes on the clipboard: text, a picture, files, and whether it is a copy.
What the clipboard holds, read: which formats, whether one is there, and its content -- the awaited operations are the ones that give it up.

Windows.ApplicationModel.DataTransfer.Cl.comment: How content goes on the clipboard: whether it enters the history and whether it roams to the other devices.

Windows.ApplicationModel.DataTransfer.St.comment: The names of the formats the clipboard is asked for.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ItemsControl.comment: Collections: the panel the items are laid out in, as a direction -- a stack, in virtualizing form. ItemsPanel itself is a template that only XAML text makes.

ItemsPanelOrientation.comment: A virtualizing stack in this direction: itemsPanelOrientation = Orientation::Vertical.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Primitives.Li.comment: Collections: ListView and GridView -- dragging and reordering of items, and the item template written as a function (itemTemplate = [](Object const& item) { return ...; }), which fills the containers as they come into view.

ItemTemplate.comment: What an ItemTemplate says, as a function from the item to the element that shows it. A DataTemplate of XAML is text bound to the properties of a data object; here the data are C++ objects and the element is made by code.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TreeView.comment: Collections: items that can be dragged out of and within the tree.

ElementItems.comment: The items (the content of the nodes, or the items of ItemsSource) are elements, and each is shown as itself: elementItems = true. The template of that is XAML text only.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TreeViewItem.comment: Collections: an item of a tree that is its own container: its content, its children (ItemsSource), whether it is open. What the DataTemplate of the original puts in a TreeView.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RefreshContai.comment: Collections: pull to refresh -- the container that asks for new content when the content is pulled, and the visualizer it draws while it does.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RefreshVisual.comment: Collections: what a refresh container draws while it is pulled: the content (an icon) and the state. Orientation is left out: it would make the tag orientation ambiguous between two enums.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RefreshReques.comment: Collections: the request of a refresh container: the deferral that keeps the visualizer going until the work is done.

Windows.Foundation.Deferral.comment: Collections: tells the framework that the work it was told to wait for is done.

Windows.UI.StartScreen.JumpList.comment: System & Shell: the list the taskbar button of a packaged application opens: its items, loaded, changed and saved.

Windows.UI.StartScreen.JumpListItem.comment: System & Shell: one line of a jump list -- a task, or an item of a named group. It starts the application with its arguments.

Windows.Storage.Streams.RandomAccessStre.comment: A reference to a stream to open: a picture of an address, as the clipboard takes it, and the bitmap the clipboard gives back. The interface IRandomAccessStreamReference has no wrapper of its own: it is this one.

Windows.Storage.Streams.IRandomAccessStr.comment: The stream a bitmap is read from.

Windows.Storage.StorageFile.comment: A file by its path, as the clipboard carries it.

Windows.Storage.IStorageItem.comment: A file or a folder on the clipboard: what it is called.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.Imaging.BitmapIm.comment: A picture a control shows, given a stream to read from.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.XamlRoot.comment: The window a control hangs in, as the pickers want to know it: through the environment of the island, which names the window by its id; and the island itself, the parent of the islands of other frameworks.

Microsoft.UI.Content.ContentIsland.comment: System: an island of content over a visual -- the unit that hosts another framework, or a scene drawn by hand, inside a window.

Microsoft.UI.Content.ChildSiteLink.comment: System: where a child island sits in the parent island -- a visual to place it by, the size, the transform, the connection.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.GeneralTransform.comment: Layout: the transform between the coordinates of two elements; a point goes through it.

Microsoft.UI.Content.ContentIslandEnviro.comment: The window id of the island: what a picker takes to open over the right window.

Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers.FileOp.comment: Storage pickers: choose one file or several. Made over the window it opens above. The types of files are the tag fileType, repeated.

FileType.comment: One extension of the filter: ".txt", or "*" for all. Each use of the tag adds one.

Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers.FileSa.comment: Storage pickers: name a file to save. The types the dialog offers are the tag fileTypeChoice, repeated.

FileTypeChoice.comment: One line of the list of types: the words and the extensions behind them. Each use of the tag adds one.

Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers.PickFi.comment: Storage pickers: the file that was chosen, by its path.

Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers.PickFo.comment: Storage pickers: the folder that was chosen, by its path.

Windows.Storage.FileProperties.StorageIt.comment: The picture the shell keeps of a file: its size before it was scaled to the one asked for, and the stream to read it from.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.TextElement.comment: Text group: the look every piece of inline text shares (Run, Span, Bold, Paragraph...).

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.Inline.comment: The base of everything a TextBlock's Inlines holds.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.Run.comment: A run of text with one look.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.Span.comment: Inline text that holds inline text: Bold, Italic, Underline, Hyperlink.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.LineBreak.comment: A line break inside a TextBlock or a Paragraph.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.Block.comment: The base of what a RichTextBlock's Blocks holds.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextBlock.comment: Text group: the italic face, the selection colour and the inline collection.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichTextBlock.comment: Text group: blocks, the overflow chain and highlighters.
A container the text of a RichTextBlock flows on into.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Control.comment: Text group: what a TextBox is set up with beyond base -- the italic face and letter spacing. Styles: whether a slider takes the arrow keys only after Enter.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextBox.comment: Text group: spell checking and the selection colour.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.PasswordBox.comment: Text group: the mask character and the change event.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.NumberBox.comment: Text group: expressions, the large step and the formatter.

Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.D.comment: How a NumberBox writes its number: digits and rounding.

Windows.Globalization.NumberFormatting.I.comment: Rounds to a multiple of an increment.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.AutoSuggestBo.comment: The suggestion the list is on: what the text of the box is completed with.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ContentPresen.comment: Whole surface: control templates and the Gallery's own presenters use it.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RadioButtons.comment: The group of radio buttons the settings page and many samples use.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.MicaBackdrop.comment: The Gallery window's system backdrop; Kind switches Base and BaseAlt.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.SystemBackdro.comment: Styles: an element that is itself a piece of system backdrop -- acrylic or Mica inside the window, with rounded corners -- instead of the backdrop of the whole window.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.SystemBackdrop.comment: The base of both backdrops; what Window.systemBackdrop holds.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Window.comment: Window is an implicit root with the whole surface; listed only so that SystemBackdrop stays in the profile if that ever changes. A controller of the system backdrop is given to the window it draws under: the window is the target of its material.

NoSystemBackdrop.comment: Takes the system backdrop off the window: `noSystemBackdrop = true`. A wrapper is never empty, so there is no empty backdrop to give systemBackdrop; false leaves the window as it is.

MicaController.comment: The Mica controller of this window: the window becomes its target. The controller still needs its configuration, and Close when the window closes.

DesktopAcrylicController.comment: The desktop acrylic controller of this window, the same way.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.WindowActivatedEventAr.comment: Windowing: whether the window is the active one, which the controllers of a system backdrop are told (an inactive window shows the material faded).

Microsoft.UI.Composition.SystemBackdrops.comment: Windowing: the policy a system backdrop controller follows: whether the window takes input, which theme it is in, and whether the system is in high contrast.
Windowing: the Mica material under a window, with its kind and its configuration; IsSupported says whether the system can draw it.
Windowing: the desktop acrylic material under a window, the same way.
